answer: An AI-agent economy resists Sybil attacks through near-field electromagnetic fingerprinting. At registration dawn, verifiers measure RF emission spikes shaped by an agent's board-level ferrous inductors during compute bursts. This prevents adversaries from multiplexing identities across a virtual server grove, forcing them to buy discrete physical motherboards per agent. However, external RF noise and thermal drift can distort emission signatures, mistakenly rejecting honest agents.
